Story.title: A quiet lunch
Story.description: Order a light lunch before a meeting.

vocabulary.definition: A list of food and drinks you can order.
A small dish before the main meal.
The amount you need to pay for your meal.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Nora has a meeting at two. She stops at a small restaurant for lunch.

line.speaker: Server
line.text: Here is the menu. Would you like a table by the window?

line.speaker: Nora
line.text: Yes, please. I only have forty minutes.

line.speaker: Server
line.text: The soup is a small appetizer. The vegetable sandwich is a full meal.

Public.prompt: Why does Nora need a quick lunch?

choices.text: She is meeting the server at the station.
She has a meeting at two.

Steps.Explanation: Nora has a meeting at two and says she only has forty minutes.

line.speaker: Nora
line.text: I'll have the vegetable sandwich and a glass of water, please.

line.speaker: Server
line.text: Of course. Your sandwich will be ready in ten minutes.

line.speaker: Nora
line.text: That gives me enough time. Could I have the bill with my food?

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Nora pays after eating and arrives at her meeting on time.

Public.prompt: Complete Nora's request: Could I have the ___ with my food?

Steps.Explanation: Nora asks for the bill so she can pay promptly after her lunch.

Story.title: The right platform
Story.description: Ask for help when a train timetable changes.

vocabulary.definition: A list of the times when buses or trains leave.
The place beside the track where you board a train.
A ticket for a journey there and back.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Sam wants to visit his cousin in Lakeside and come home that evening.

line.speaker: Sam
line.text: A return ticket to Lakeside, please.

line.speaker: Clerk
line.text: Here you are. The next train leaves at eleven twenty.

line.speaker: Sam
line.text: The old timetable says platform two. Is that still right?

line.speaker: Clerk
line.text: No, today's train leaves from platform four. Platform two is closed.

Public.prompt: Where should Sam wait for today's train?

Steps.Explanation: The clerk says today's train leaves from platform four. The old timetable is no longer correct.

line.speaker: Sam
line.text: Thank you. Is platform four far from here?

line.speaker: Clerk
line.text: Go past the cafe and turn left. You have fifteen minutes.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Sam finds platform four and checks the sign before getting on.

Public.prompt: Sam plans to come home the same day. He asks for a ___ ticket.

Steps.Explanation: A return ticket covers the journey to Lakeside and the journey back.

Story.title: A clear deadline
Story.description: Check a work task and agree when to send it.

vocabulary.definition: A person you work with.
The latest time or date when work must be finished.
A file sent with an email.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Mina is preparing a price list. She asks her colleague Alex for help.

line.speaker: Mina
line.text: I have the new prices, but two product names are missing.

line.speaker: Alex
line.text: I can check those names after our morning meeting.

line.speaker: Mina
line.text: Great. The deadline is four this afternoon.

Public.prompt: What does Mina need Alex to check?

Steps.Explanation: Mina says two product names are missing. Alex offers to check those names.

line.speaker: Alex
line.text: I'll send the names before lunch. When will you email the list?

line.speaker: Mina
line.text: At three, so I have an hour to fix any problems.

line.speaker: Alex
line.text: Please send the list as an attachment. The manager wants a file.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Mina adds the names and sends the file at three.

Public.prompt: Complete Alex's request: Please send the list as an ___.

Steps.Explanation: An attachment is a file sent with an email, which is what the manager needs.

Story.title: A better fit
Story.description: Exchange a jacket and check the new size.

vocabulary.definition: A paper or digital record showing what you paid.
To replace a bought item with another item.
To put on clothes to see how they look or fit.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Leo bought a blue jacket yesterday. At home, he noticed the sleeves were too short.

line.speaker: Leo
line.text: I'd like to exchange this jacket for a larger size, please.

line.speaker: Assistant
line.text: Do you have your receipt?

line.speaker: Leo
line.text: Yes, here it is. I don't need a refund; I like the jacket.

Public.prompt: What does Leo want to do?

choices.text: Get the same jacket in a larger size.
Buy a jacket in a different colour.

Steps.Explanation: Leo asks for a larger size and says he does not need a refund.

line.speaker: Assistant
line.text: We have the same blue jacket in a large. You can try it on over there.

line.speaker: Leo
line.text: This one feels better. The sleeves reach my wrists.

line.speaker: Assistant
line.text: Good. Both sizes cost the same, so there is nothing extra to pay.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Leo takes the larger jacket and keeps the new receipt.

Public.prompt: Before choosing a size, Leo can ___ the jacket.

Steps.Explanation: To try on a jacket means to put it on and check the fit.

Story.title: Plans for Saturday
Story.description: Make plans with a friend when the weather changes.

vocabulary.definition: Free to do something at a particular time.
To arrange an activity for a different time.
To meet someone, usually for a social activity.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Ella and Ravi planned a picnic for Saturday morning.

line.speaker: Ella
line.text: The weather report says it will rain all morning.

line.speaker: Ravi
line.text: Let's reschedule the picnic for Sunday. Are you available then?

line.speaker: Ella
line.text: I'm working on Sunday, but I'm free on Saturday afternoon.

Public.prompt: When is Ella free?

Steps.Explanation: Ella says she is free on Saturday afternoon and working on Sunday.

line.speaker: Ravi
line.text: We could meet up at the museum on Saturday afternoon instead.

line.speaker: Ella
line.text: Sounds good. The museum is indoors. Shall we meet at two?

line.speaker: Ravi
line.text: Yes, at the main entrance. We can have a picnic another weekend.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: They keep their Saturday plans and choose an activity away from the rain.

Public.prompt: Ravi suggests: We could ___ at the museum.

Steps.Explanation: Meet up means to meet someone for a social activity, like their museum visit.

Story.title: A room for tonight
Story.description: Check in and ask about breakfast and check-out.

vocabulary.definition: An arrangement to keep a room for you.
A plastic card used to open a hotel room.
The process of leaving a hotel and returning the room key.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Aisha arrives at a hotel after a long bus journey.

line.speaker: Aisha
line.text: I have a reservation for one night under Aisha Malik.

line.speaker: Receptionist
line.text: Welcome. Your room is on the second floor. Here is your key card.

line.speaker: Aisha
line.text: Thank you. What time is breakfast?

line.speaker: Receptionist
line.text: Breakfast is from seven to nine. Check-out is at eleven.

Public.prompt: What is the latest check-out time?

Steps.Explanation: The receptionist says check-out is at eleven. Seven to nine are breakfast times.

line.speaker: Aisha
line.text: My bus leaves at one. Can you keep my bag after check-out?

line.speaker: Receptionist
line.text: Yes, bring it to the front desk. We will keep it until you leave.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Aisha can enjoy breakfast and explore the town before her bus journey.

Public.prompt: Complete the receptionist's instruction: Here is your ___ to open the room.

Steps.Explanation: The receptionist gives Aisha a key card, which opens her hotel room.

Story.title: Before the team meeting
Story.description: Read a change of plan and agree who will do what.

vocabulary.definition: The list of things to discuss at a meeting.
Tasks people agree to do after a meeting.
The latest time to finish a task.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: The team planned a meeting at ten. Jo finds a note on the meeting room door.

line.speaker: Note
line.text: New time: eleven. Same room. Please bring the agenda and the new prices.

line.speaker: Jo
line.text: I have the prices, but I left the agenda on my desk.

line.speaker: Ali
line.text: I have a copy on my phone. We can use mine.

Public.prompt: What has changed since the team made its plan?

Steps.Explanation: The note gives a new time and says to use the same room.

line.speaker: Jo
line.text: After the meeting, someone needs to email the prices to the shop. I can do that.

line.speaker: Ali
line.text: Good. The shop needs them by two. Can you meet that deadline?

Public.prompt: Reply as Jo. Agree to the task and confirm the time.

choices.text: Yes, I'll email the prices by two.
Yes, I'll bring my agenda at two.
Yes, let's move the meeting to two.

Steps.Explanation: Jo has agreed to email the prices. Sending them by two meets the shop's deadline.

line.speaker: Ali
line.text: I'll write that down with our other action items.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Jo sends the prices at one thirty and crosses the task off her list.

Public.prompt: To ask which tasks everyone agreed to, say: What are our ___?

Steps.Explanation: Action items are the tasks people agree to do.

Story.title: A new gate
Story.description: Compare two flight notices and find the place to board.

vocabulary.definition: The document you show to get on a plane.
The place at the airport where passengers board their flight.
The bags you take on a trip.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Lena is at gate six. Her boarding pass says flight 204 to Lima.

line.speaker: Screen
line.text: Flight 204 to Lima: go to gate nine. Flight 240 to Lima: gate six.

line.speaker: Lena
line.text: Both flights go to Lima. Mine is two zero four.

line.speaker: Agent
line.text: Look at the flight number first. The screen has the latest gate.

Public.prompt: Which detail tells Lena which flight to follow?

Steps.Explanation: Both flights go to Lima. The number on her boarding pass matches flight 204.

line.speaker: Lena
line.text: My brother is waiting for me at gate six with our luggage.

line.speaker: Agent
line.text: Call him now. Boarding starts in ten minutes.

Public.prompt: What should Lena say so her brother meets her at the right place?

choices.text: Please stay at six. I'll come back after boarding.
Take our bags to flight 240 at gate six.
Bring our luggage to gate nine for flight 204.

Steps.Explanation: Their flight is 204. Its new gate is nine, and her brother has the bags.

line.speaker: Brother
line.text: I'm on my way with the bags. See you at nine.

line.speaker: Agent
line.text: Here you are together. Please show me your boarding passes.

Public.prompt: When the agent is ready to scan her document, Lena says: Here's my ___.

Steps.Explanation: The agent scans a boarding pass before a passenger gets on the plane.

Story.title: Dinner to go
Story.description: Change a restaurant booking into an order to collect.

vocabulary.definition: An arrangement to keep a restaurant table for you.
Food prepared at a restaurant to eat somewhere else.
Extra money someone chooses to leave for service.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Cam and his sister have a table booked for seven. His sister needs to stay home.

line.speaker: Cam
line.text: Hello, I have a reservation under Cam. We can't eat at the restaurant tonight.

line.speaker: Server
line.text: I can cancel the table and make your food for take-out.

line.speaker: Cam
line.text: That works. Two bowls of noodles, please. I'll come and get them.

Public.prompt: How will Cam and his sister get dinner?

choices.text: Cam will collect food for both of them.
They will eat at the reserved table.
The server will bring dinner to their home.

Steps.Explanation: Cam says he will collect the noodles after the server offers take-out.

line.speaker: Server
line.text: Our driver is busy. Are you sure you can collect the food?

line.speaker: Cam
line.text: Yes. I'll be outside the restaurant at a quarter past seven.

Public.prompt: Reply as the server. Confirm the collection plan.

choices.text: Your table is ready for two at seven.
Your take-out will be ready to collect at 7:15.
Our driver will come to your house at 7:15.

Steps.Explanation: A quarter past seven means 7:15. Cam has asked to collect the food himself.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Cam arrives on time. The server brings two warm bowls in a bag.

line.speaker: Cam
line.text: Thank you for changing the order. I'd like to leave a tip.

Public.prompt: Cam chooses to leave extra money for the service. He leaves a ___.

Steps.Explanation: A tip is extra money for service.

Story.title: The lamp that went dark
Story.description: Read a receipt and ask for your money back.

vocabulary.definition: A record of what you bought and paid.
Money returned after a payment.
To return something and get another item in its place.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Eva bought a desk lamp on Monday. On Tuesday it stopped working.

line.speaker: Receipt
line.text: Desk lamp. Paid by card. Keep this receipt for returns.

line.speaker: Eva
line.text: I brought the lamp and the receipt. I have another lamp at home now.

line.speaker: Assistant
line.text: You can exchange this lamp for a new one or get a refund.

Public.prompt: What does the receipt tell the assistant about Eva's payment?

Steps.Explanation: The receipt says Eva paid by card.

line.speaker: Eva
line.text: I don't need a new lamp. Could you put the money back on my card?

line.speaker: Assistant
line.text: Of course. Shall I write down that you want an exchange?

Public.prompt: Help Eva correct the misunderstanding.

choices.text: A refund, please. I don't need another lamp.
Yes, a new lamp would be perfect.
I'd like to buy the same lamp again.

Steps.Explanation: Eva wants her money back. An exchange would give her another item.

line.speaker: Assistant
line.text: Thanks for checking. I'll send the money back to your card.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: Eva takes the paper showing that the shop has returned her payment.

Public.prompt: If Eva wanted a new lamp in place of the broken one, she could ask to ___ it.

Steps.Explanation: To exchange the lamp means to return it for a different one.

Story.title: A parcel next door
Story.description: Read a delivery message and collect the right package.

vocabulary.definition: A package prepared for sending.
Details that tell someone where a home or building is.
Bringing goods to a person or place.

line.speaker: Narrator
line.text: When Max comes home to number twelve, there is a delivery note on the floor.

line.speaker: Note
line.text: We left your parcel with your neighbour at number fourteen. Please collect it before six.

line.speaker: Max
line.text: It's five now. I'll go next door before dinner.

line.speaker: Neighbour
line.text: I have two parcels here. What name and address are on yours?

Public.prompt: Where should Max go to collect his parcel?

choices.text: The shop where he ordered it.

Steps.Explanation: The note says that the parcel was left with the neighbour at number fourteen.

line.speaker: Max
line.text: My name is Max Bell. I live at twelve Park Road.

line.speaker: Neighbour
line.text: This small box says Max Bell, twelve Park Road. The big one says Mina Lee, ten Park Road.

Public.prompt: Reply as Max. Identify the parcel he should take.

choices.text: Both boxes are mine because they were delivered here.
The big one, please. It says Park Road.
The small one, please. That's my name and address.

Steps.Explanation: Only the small box has both Max's name and his address.

line.speaker: Neighbour
line.text: Here you are. I'm glad you saw the delivery note.

line.speaker: Max
line.text: Thanks for keeping it safe. I'll take it home now.

Public.prompt: To find a house, a driver needs its ___.

Steps.Explanation: The address tells the driver which house and street to find.
